publication_title: Efficacy and Safety of Vismodegib in Advanced Basal-Cell Carcinoma
evidence_relationship: Pivotal single-arm trial with separately labelled follow-up analyses
evidence_context: Advanced basal cell carcinoma: metastatic and locally advanced cohorts; interpret against the exact NCCP adult indication.
study_design: International, multicentre, open-label phase II study with two nonrandomised cohorts and no control arm.
trial_population: 104 patients treated: 33 metastatic and 71 locally advanced BCC. Efficacy analyses included 33 metastatic and 63 locally advanced cases after independent pathology review. Adults had ECOG 0-2 and adequate organ function; locally advanced disease was inoperable or surgery was inappropriate, with radiotherapy previously unsuccessful, contraindicated or inappropriate.
intervention: Vismodegib 150 mg orally once daily until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal.
comparator: None. The primary analysis tested ORR against prespecified null rates of 10% for metastatic and 20% for locally advanced BCC; these thresholds are not a treatment-control group.
primary_endpoint: Independently assessed, confirmed objective response (complete or partial). Metastatic BCC used RECIST 1.0. Locally advanced BCC used a composite of external/radiographic lesion reduction or ulceration resolution without progression, with biopsy contributing to complete-response classification; response confirmation required at least four weeks.
relevance_summary: Supports tumour-response activity in eligible advanced BCC. The current EMA summary reports an independent-review update 21 months after the final enrolment and a distinct investigator-assessed analysis 39 months after final enrolment.
match_type: Same drug and advanced BCC disease settings; maintain the exact NCCP eligibility criteria and do not extrapolate these response rates to routine resectable BCC.
key_findings: Primary analysis, November 2010 (9 months after the last enrolment), independent review: 10/33 metastatic cases responded (30.3%, reported as 30% in the original paper); 27/63 locally advanced cases responded (42.9%, reported as 43%). Median response duration was 7.6 months in each cohort.

EMA Table 2 independent-review analysis, 21 months after the last enrolment (the 12-month update of the primary analysis): metastatic ORR 11/33, 33.3% (95% CI 19.2-51.8%); locally advanced ORR 30/63, 47.6% (95% CI 35.5-60.6%).
At that same 21-month independent-review analysis, median response duration was 7.6 months in metastatic and 9.5 months in locally advanced BCC; complete responses were 0/33 and 14/63, respectively.

Later 39-month analysis after the last enrolment used investigator assessment: metastatic ORR 16/33, 48.5% (95% CI 30.8-66.2%); locally advanced ORR 38/63, 60.3% (95% CI 47.2-71.7%). These are not independent-review results.
At the 39-month investigator analysis, median response duration was 14.8 and 26.2 months, respectively. These descriptive durations do not establish superiority over another treatment.
limitations: Single-arm evidence with no randomised comparator cannot establish a comparative survival benefit or cure rate. The two cohorts used different response assessments and must remain separate. Analyses use 96 efficacy-evaluable patients, rather than all 104 treated patients; eight locally advanced cases were excluded after independent pathology review. The small cohorts, selected ECOG 0-2 population and entirely White study population limit generalisability. Longer follow-up and investigator review do not make the later percentages interchangeable with the independent primary endpoint.
review_status: Primary and regulatory source reconciliation complete; independent clinical and pharmacy review pending
